name: ISO 9001 (Quality Management Systems)
description: Requirements for a quality management system, structured on the Annex SL high-level structure (clauses 4 to 10) and built on the process approach, risk-based thinking and the Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle. Frequently required for ICI, institutional and public-sector prequalification. For a trade contractor the clauses that carry the most audit weight are 8.5 (production and service provision), 8.7 (nonconforming outputs), 7.1.5 (monitoring and measuring resources) and 10.2 (corrective action) — these are where inspection, test and handover records live.
scope: Any organization seeking to demonstrate consistent provision of conforming products and services

families.name: Clause 4 — Context of the Organization
families.description: Scope of the management system and the processes that make it up.

controls.name: Understanding the Organization and Its Context
controls.description: External and internal issues relevant to the quality management system are determined, monitored and reviewed.

controls.name: Scope of the Quality Management System
controls.description: The boundaries and applicability of the QMS are documented, including any requirement determined not applicable and the justification.

controls.name: Quality Management System and Its Processes
controls.description: Required processes are determined with their inputs, outputs, sequence, criteria, responsibilities and performance indicators.

families.name: Clause 5 — Leadership
families.description: Top-management accountability, quality policy and assigned responsibility.

controls.name: Leadership and Commitment (including Customer Focus)
controls.description: Top management demonstrates accountability for the QMS and ensures customer and applicable statutory requirements are determined and met.

controls.name: Quality Policy
controls.description: A quality policy is established, documented, communicated within the organization and available to interested parties.

controls.name: Organizational Roles, Responsibilities and Authorities
controls.description: Responsibilities and authorities for the QMS are assigned, communicated and understood.

families.name: Clause 6 — Planning
families.description: Risk-based thinking, quality objectives and planned change.

controls.name: Actions to Address Risks and Opportunities
controls.description: Risks and opportunities affecting conformity and customer satisfaction are determined, with planned actions integrated into the QMS and their effectiveness evaluated.

controls.name: Quality Objectives and Planning to Achieve Them
controls.description: Measurable quality objectives are set at relevant levels, with what will be done, by whom, when, and how results are evaluated.

controls.name: Planning of Changes
controls.description: Changes to the QMS are carried out in a planned manner, considering consequences, resource availability and reallocation of responsibilities.

families.name: Clause 7 — Support
families.description: Resources, competence, calibration and documented information.

controls.name: Monitoring and Measuring Resources (Calibration)
controls.description: Measuring equipment is suitable, verified or calibrated against traceable standards at defined intervals, identified with its status, and safeguarded from adjustment.

controls.name: Organizational Knowledge
controls.description: Knowledge necessary for process operation and conformity is determined, maintained and made available.

controls.name: Competence
controls.description: Competence is determined per role, acquired where lacking, and the basis of competence is retained as documented information.

controls.name: Documented Information
controls.description: Documented information is controlled: identified, reviewed and approved, version-controlled, available where needed, and protected from unintended alteration.

families.name: Clause 8 — Operation
families.description: Where a contractor's quality system is actually tested: requirements review, external providers, service provision, release and nonconforming output.

controls.name: Requirements for Products and Services
controls.description: Customer requirements including statutory, regulatory and contract requirements are determined and reviewed before commitment, and changes are recorded.

controls.name: Control of Externally Provided Processes, Products and Services
controls.description: Suppliers and subcontractors are evaluated and selected against criteria, controls are applied proportionate to impact, and performance is re-evaluated.

controls.name: Production and Service Provision
controls.description: Work is carried out under controlled conditions with available specifications, suitable equipment, competent personnel, and identification and traceability of output.

controls.name: Release of Products and Services
controls.description: Work is not released until planned verification is complete, with evidence of conformity and the authority who released it recorded.

controls.name: Control of Nonconforming Outputs
controls.description: Nonconforming work is identified and controlled to prevent unintended use, with correction, concession or rework recorded along with the authority deciding.

families.name: Clause 9 — Performance Evaluation
families.description: Measurement, customer satisfaction, internal audit and management review.

controls.name: Monitoring, Measurement, Analysis and Evaluation
controls.description: Performance and effectiveness of the QMS are monitored against defined methods and intervals, including customer satisfaction, and results are analysed.

controls.name: Internal Audit
controls.description: Internal audits are conducted on a risk-based programme by objective auditors, with results reported to management and nonconformities corrected.

controls.name: Management Review
controls.description: Top management reviews the QMS at planned intervals against defined inputs, with documented decisions on improvement, change and resource need.

controls.name: Nonconformity and Corrective Action
controls.description: Nonconformities are reacted to, their causes evaluated, corrective action taken and its effectiveness reviewed, with the nature of the nonconformity and results retained.

controls.name: Continual Improvement
controls.description: The suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the QMS are continually improved, informed by analysis, evaluation and management review output.
